evidence: SOURCE REVIEW (Pass). Dimensions run one after another on one app process and one database: tests/test.sh runs `run_suite gates 1500` then `run_suite scored 11100`, each with `rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1`, with no database reset in between (test.sh is byte-identical to the frozen template). The seed is empty (environment/assets/seed_data.json: `"snippets": []`), so there are no seeded values a later dimension could expect to find untouched. tests/app_context.md line 24, injected into all five prompts, states the state-relative rule directly: "Saved records are identified by the server, not by title, and the library may already hold records from earlier checks. Do not assume an empty library and do not delete records that earlier checks created." Line 23 adds "Use fresh scratch drafts for editor checks." and line 28 "After the restart tool has been used, open fresh pages instead of reusing pages opened before the restart." Every criterion that touches saved data builds its own record and counts relative to it: gates/constraints cw_shared_saved_record "Create one new .js snippet with a unique title ... Leave the saved record in place"; functional cw_save_reload_restart "give it an exact unique title and filename ... the same single record"; cw_stale_save_refused "exactly one new revision"; cw_history_restore_retry "Build three saved revisions of one snippet"; cw_restore_request_repeat_safe "exactly three revisions for the snippet"; cw_live_library_update "the new title must appear"; cw_preview_isolation "save one snippet with a unique title" plus a judge-chosen hostile marker; polish cw_undo_redo_availability and cw_unsaved_marker each "Save a snippet" of their own. I found no criterion or prompt that asserts an empty library, a total record count, a first/only record, a particular list position or a seeded value (grep for seed/empty/pristine/first record/only record over tests/ returns only the tolerant app_context line). Browser-side state cannot leak across dimensions: every judge.toml starts playwright-mcp with `--isolated`, so localStorage set or cleared in one dimension (constraints and functional both clear storage; functional sets one localStorage entry) is not seen by the next. The one process restart happens inside functional (cw_save_reload_restart) on the same DB_PATH; polish and visual prompts only require the app to load and the editor to take typing, which a restarted app satisfies. The visual prompt prepares its own state ("put a ten-line JavaScript draft in the editor and Run it once") rather than relying on an initial screen. Broken-app probe: an app that lost or duplicated earlier records is still caught, because the per-record checks are identified by unique title and by that record's own revision count. Conforming-alternative probe: an app whose library is long after about ten to fifteen accumulated records is not failed by any count or position assumption. NOTES (not defects in this row). (a) Visual cw_visual_workspace_layout and polish cw_controls_keyboard_and_focus / cw_narrow_width_usable are judged with the library already holding the records left by gates and functional; the criteria do not say so explicitly, but they do not assume emptiness either, and the golden bounds the library (style.css `.library{max-height:36%}` with overflow auto). (b) cw_controls_keyboard_and_focus asks the judge to move through the library by keyboard; with accumulated records this costs more key presses than on an empty library - a workload point for the timing rows, not a pristine-seed assumption. EVIDENCE GAP (reason for risk=true). No run of the configured judges exists for these bytes, so the sequential gates -> functional -> polish -> visual behaviour on a mutated database is not measured for this candidate. In addition I could not verify any artifact cited in raw-evidence-index.json: at review time (2 Oct 2026, about 20:27-20:30 IST) all 22 indexed paths were absent from disk - qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-10-02-strict/ contained only results/build.log and results/restart.log (no run_golden.sh, no tests/*.cjs, no results/*.json or *.png), and the two hosted-run directories contained only trial.log, job.log and an empty verifier tree (no result.json, reward.json or reward-details.json). None of these files is tracked by git. The index's claims (scripted golden 3 gate + 43 Functional + 6 Polish; hosted Oracle 0.9833 on an earlier candidate) are therefore unverified by me and are not used as support for this verdict. The Pass rests on source reading only.
